A pending ship gate also carries `blockers`: each has a `kind` (`merge_conflict`, `ci` with the `checks` by name, `unverified_build`, `refinement_not_applied`), a `detail` sentence and `blocks` (`everyone`, or `api_keys` when only a person in the Console may approve). Read it before anyforge_submit_approval: an approval with a blocker is refused. The default response stays under ~20 KB; ask for more with `include`. Reviewer verdicts (`architectVerdict`, `securityVerdict`, `qaVerdict`) come with `<field>Label`, the word the Console shows, and `<field>Outcome` (`clean`, `non_blocking` or `blocking`). `NEEDS_REVISION` is non-blocking and the Console labels it "Advisory"; the Console's "Needs revision" means the blocking `FAIL`.

Requires a key with the `approve` scope.

autoMerge.description: Ship gate approvals only: true merges the pull request once checks are green on the approved head; false approves without merging. Omit to use the gate's own setting (its autoMergeOnApproval). An initiative that leaves pull requests for human review is never merged.

tools.name: anyforge_list_work_items
tools.description: List work items in the AnyForge backlog with status, priority, and any linked crew state. ONE PAGE per call (50 by default, 200 max), newest first: the result carries `total` (matches for THESE filters across every page), `hasMore`, `nextCursor`, `appliedFilters` (the filters that actually ran — check it when `total` surprises you) and `nextAction`. When `hasMore` is true, pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` with the SAME filters for the next page. A page with no relevant rows says nothing about the remaining pages — check `hasMore` before concluding there is no match. Narrow with `programId`, `initiativeId`, `team`, `status`, `priority`, `type`, `assignee`, `reporter`, `label` or `search` rather than paging through a whole backlog; `label` matches one exact label, such as a stage of a label group (anyforge_list_label_groups lists the groups and anyforge_list_work_boards the boards that follow them); to scope a question first, resolve the initiative with anyforge_list_initiatives, then list its items with `initiativeId`. `search` matches id, code, title, description, acceptance criteria, design notes, crew id, latest-status text, tags, component ids and the tracker key (`externalRef.key` or `jiraIssueKey`) — not lifecycle status or initiative names. By default archived items are excluded. Each item carries `assigneeName`, `blockerOwnerName` and `createdByName` beside `assigneeUid`, `blockerOwnerUid` and `createdBy`: the member's name (or email), null when the field is empty or names someone who is not an approved member.

team.description: Filter to a team's items by team slug, including every team beneath it. An item's team is the one set on it, else its initiative's. An unknown slug is refused (unknown_team).

priority.description: Filter by priority; `none` lists items with no priority.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle status.

itemId.description: Filter to an exact work-item id or queue code.

search.description: Search by work-item id, code, title, description, crew id or tracker key (case-insensitive substring).

label.description: Only items carrying this exact label (case-insensitive), for example one stage of a label group. A label group's name is not a label: list the groups with anyforge_list_label_groups.

owner.description: One person's work, by uid: items in initiatives they own, standalone items they filed and items assigned to them (the Console's Owner filter). Use 'me' for the API key owner.

assignee.description: Filter by human assignee uid; use 'me' for the API key owner.

reporter.description: Filter by who reported (filed) the item, by uid; use 'me' for the API key owner.

completedFrom.description: Only items completed on or after this day (yyyy-mm-dd, UTC, inclusive). An item with no recorded completion is left out. Combine with owner or assignee for what one person finished in a period, or use anyforge_get_work_summary.

completedTo.description: Only items completed on or before this day (yyyy-mm-dd, UTC, inclusive).

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous page. Only valid with identical filters.

Any member may ask about any approved member (one person at a time); it lists only items the caller can already read. Archived items count. Find the uid with anyforge_list_members. Requires `read` scope.

person.description: The member's uid; 'me' for the API key owner.

from.description: First day of the period, yyyy-mm-dd (UTC, inclusive).

to.description: Last day of the period, yyyy-mm-dd (UTC, inclusive).

by.description: Whose work counts: 'owner' (default; items assigned to them, items in initiatives they own and standalone items they filed) or 'assignee' (only items assigned to them).

A board whose columns follow a label group carries `labelColumns.labelGroupId` and `columnLabels`, the stage labels in column order; list the cards of one column with anyforge_list_work_items and `label`. Boards are a view over work items, not work items, so a search of the work items never finds a board or a label group by name.

tools.name: anyforge_create_work_item
tools.description: Create a new work item in the backlog (status BACKLOG). Requires `write` scope.

tags.description: Labels for the new item (the Console's Labels field). Labels are trimmed, lower-cased and deduplicated; at most 20 per item, 40 characters each. A label in one of the workspace's label groups replaces the item's other label from that group.

priority.description: P0 is highest priority; `none` files the item with no priority.

allowedWritePaths.description: File write scope: a hard boundary on the repository files the crew may change, as relative patterns (literal, * or **; [ and ] are literal characters, so src/pages/[slug].astro is a valid entry). null/omitted is unrestricted; [] is read-only. Any write scope also withholds connected (MCP) tools that can write; tools their server marks readOnlyHint stay. Set before dispatch. Locked while the attached crew can still run; once it has halted or finished, send it alone in an update to change it, then retry the item. To point the crew at a monorepo folder without restricting it, use folderScope.

assigneeUid.description: Human executor — an approved editor+ member, by uid or email (anyforge_list_members lists both). Files the item for a person; it still lands in BACKLOG until `begin`.

externalRef.description: Where this work lives in another system, the same shape the item's externalRef reads back. Do not send it with externalId or dedupeByExternalId.

key.description: The id in the other system: a tracker key such as PROJ-42, or a CRM record id.

url.description: Optional http(s) link to the record in the other system.

dedupe.description: When an item in the workspace already carries this key, return it (existing: true) instead of filing a second one. Nothing is written. Use it when the same request may be sent again. Default false.

inTitle.description: false files the title as written; true or absent shows the key in the title as [KEY] - title. Use false for an opaque record id.

createdAt.description: When the record was created in the other system: yyyy-mm-dd, or an ISO time with a zone. Send it when mirroring existing work, so capacity counts the work as arriving then, not on the day it was filed here.

resolvedAt.description: When the record was resolved in the other system: yyyy-mm-dd, or an ISO time with a zone. Send it when mirroring finished work, so it counts as finished then. Not before createdAt.

externalId.description: Legacy: use externalRef.key. The id this work has in another system, shown in the title as [ID].

dedupeByExternalId.description: Legacy: use externalRef.dedupe. With externalId, return the item that already carries it instead of filing a second one.

estimate.description: Effort estimate as a person says it — "2h", "1.5d", "1w", or a number of days. Stored as operator-days.

estimatePoints.description: Point estimate on the point scale this workspace uses (Fibonacci, linear, exponential, or a T-shirt size such as "M"). Refused while the workspace estimates in time. Points never feed capacity plans.

dependsOn.description: Work-item ids that must finish first.

classOfService.description: File this as an interrupt in the expedite lane.

branchName.description: Branch this item's crew works on, instead of the name derived from the workspace's branch naming (for example feature/csv-export). Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-' and '/'; not main, master or another integration branch. An expedited item still uses the hotfix prefix unless this name starts with it.

continuesPullRequest.description: When this work continues an open pull request, its link (https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number}) in the item's repository. AnyForge reads the pull request and sets the item's branch to its head and its base branch to its base, so the crew commits to that pull request instead of opening a new one. Use this instead of naming the branch or pull request in the description: a crew only works on the branch the item names. Refused when the pull request is merged, closed, from a fork or in another repository.

folderScope.description: Repository folder this item's work is in, for a monorepo (for example apps/web), or a list when it spans several (for example ["apps/api", "apps/web"]). The crew installs the first folder's Node project, is told to work there, runs tests from it by default, and gets that folder's repository skills first; it is told the work also touches the others and gets their skills next. It restricts nothing and withholds no tools: to limit which files the crew may change, use allowedWritePaths. Not targetPath, which is migration only.

targetGithubRepo.description: Repository this item will modify; must be one of the initiative's repositories. To scope the work to a folder, use folderScope, not targetPath.

serviceId.description: One of the initiative's services (its id, from get_initiative), when it declares them. The item's repository must be the service's; the service's folder becomes the item's folderScope.

targetGithubBranch.description: Base branch this item's crew branches from and opens its pull request against (for example feature/x), instead of the initiative's source branch. Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-' and '/'; an integration branch such as develop is allowed here. It must exist on the remote: dispatch fails with base_branch_missing, naming it, rather than falling back to the initiative's branch. Not the head branch: use branchName for that. When continuesPullRequest is also set, the pull request's base wins and a different value is refused.

sourceGithubRepo.description: Migration only: read-only source repository to copy from. The fields below need it.

sourceGithubBranch.description: Migration only: source branch to copy from.

sourceGithubSha.description: Migration only: source commit to copy from.

sourcePath.description: Migration only: path in the source repository to copy.

targetPath.description: Migration only: where the copied source lands in the target repository. Not a working folder for ordinary work; use folderScope for that.

migrationStrategy.description: Migration only: copy, history-preserving, or subtree.

incident.description: Incident severity and impact metadata when the item is an incident.

attachments.description: Evidence references such as URLs or storage references. Do not send raw file bytes.

reportedMilestoneId.description: Program milestone (wave) this was REPORTED against — provenance only, never scheduling. Requires an initiative that belongs to a program, and must be one of that program's milestone ids.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Reusing a key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reused. 8-120 letters, digits, "_" or "-".

tools.name: anyforge_update_work_item
tools.description: Mutate one work item. `action` is one of advance, approve_refinement, approve-and-route, move-initiative, dispatch, complete, update, reorder, archive, unarchive, close-as-fixed, reopen, mark-incident, drop, undrop, confirm-repo, assign, begin, dismiss-automation-suggestion, expedite, block, unblock, link-external, verification, add-evidence, remove-evidence, share-evidence, undefer, set-cycle, scope-change, link-pull-request, unlink-pull-request, link-work-item, unlink-work-item, set-parent, or clear-parent. Each action takes only its own fields: a field the action does not read is refused with 400 unsupported_fields, naming the field and the actions that do read it, and nothing is changed — so a success means every field you passed was applied. To move an item BACK (or between BACKLOG, REFINED and READY), send `status` with NO action: it takes BACKLOG, REFINED or READY, from one of those statuses or from work a person began (IN_PROGRESS with no crew) — the Console status menu's plain move, with the same role and initiative-steward rules, recorded in the item's history. Any other move is refused with 409 raw_status_not_allowed, naming allowedStatuses and the action to use instead (useAction): reopen for DONE, undrop for DROPPED, begin for IN_PROGRESS, complete for DONE, dispatch for a crew, drop; an item a crew carries moves with its crew. anyforge_get_work_item returns `nextActions.statusMoves`, the exact arguments for each move you may make now. Forward moves have their own actions too: advance, approve_refinement, begin, dispatch, complete. Use action='set-review' with inReview (true or false) to put work a person began (IN_PROGRESS, no crew) in or out of review; begin also takes inReview: true to start an item already in review. Use action='assign' with assigneeUid (a member uid or their email; anyforge_list_members lists both) to set the human executor. Use action='block' with blockReason (what the item is waiting on), blockCategory and optionally blockerOwnerUid (who is chasing it, uid or email) to mark an item blocked without changing its status; action='unblock' clears it. Use action='link-pull-request' with pullRequestUrl to show a GitHub pull request on the item, at any status (the Jira development panel). The pull request need not name the item; its state, title and reviewers are read from GitHub and kept current as it changes, and a linked pull request never moves the item. Pull requests that name the item by its code link themselves. action='unlink-pull-request' with the same URL removes one. Use action='set-parent' with parentWorkItemId to make another work item this item's parent (one level only: at most one parent, in an initiative of the same program). It is refused, with nothing changed, as parent_self, parent_not_found, parent_unavailable, parent_program_required, parent_other_program, parent_already_set, parent_cycle, parent_has_parent or item_has_children; action='clear-parent' removes it (a no-op when none is set). Moving an item to another initiative of the same program keeps the link; a move to another program that would separate parent and children is refused with move_separates_parent or move_separates_children. Use action='link-work-item' with linkedWorkItemId (another work item's id in this workspace, from any initiative) and linkType 'relates_to' or 'duplicates' to connect two items; action='unlink-work-item' with the same two fields removes it. Both work at any status, DONE and DROPPED included, so finished work keeps its history; they change only the link and never move, block or unblock either item. relates_to has no direction. duplicates is directional: this item duplicates linkedWorkItemId (the original), which shows it as duplicated by; the reverse is refused with duplicate_link_direction_conflict until the existing link is removed. The link is written on both items, a repeat is a no-op, an item cannot link to itself, and each item holds at most 50 typed links. anyforge_get_work_item returns them as linkedWorkItems ({ id, type, direction, code, title, status }). A 'blocks' relationship is a dependency, not a typed link: set dependsOn on the blocked item with action='update'. While a crew is building the item (IN_CREW), its acceptanceCriteria, outOfScope and dependsOn may still change when sent alone: the running crew is told, which spends no amend. Anything else on such an item, and these too once its pull request merged or the item is DONE or DROPPED, is refused with not_editable. Before set-cycle, list the cycles of the item's team (team.id) with anyforge_list_cycles: it names the current cycle and which are locked. Use action='set-cycle' with committedCycleNumber (a cycle number on the item's own team cadence, or null for none) to plan the item into a delivery cycle. A locked or ended cycle, a cycle number beyond the cadence's planning horizon, and finished work are refused with the reason (409 cycle_locked, cycle_in_past, cycle_not_found with validFrom/validTo, item_finished). To bring ONE item into a locked cycle (the current one, or one signed off early) without its initiative, use action='scope-change' with committedCycleNumber (that locked cycle) and reason (why it comes in; required). It changes only the item's cycle: its crew and status are untouched. It is recorded, with the reason, in the cycle's Scope changes log, and the result carries the team's commitment in the cycle after the change (commitment.items, commitment.demandDays) and the capacity check (capacity.availableDays, projectedDays, addedDays, overByDays, fits; null availableDays and fits when the team has no measured capacity). When it would take the team over capacity it is refused with 409 over_capacity_unconfirmed and the same numbers, and nothing changes: tell the person the overage and, only if they agree, send it again with confirmOverCapacity: true. An ended cycle is refused with cycle_in_past, a cycle that is not locked with cycle_not_locked (use set-cycle), and an item in another running locked cycle with cycle_locked (take it out first with action='descope'). It needs a credential bound to a person whose role edits work items; otherwise 403 insufficient_role. The item already in the cycle is answered with changed: false and nothing is recorded again. To take ONE item out of the locked cycle it is in without its initiative, use action='descope' with reason (why it leaves; required) and committedCycleNumber (where it goes: a later cycle that is not locked, or null or omitted for no cycle). It changes only the item's cycle: its crew and status are untouched. It is recorded, with the reason and destination, in the cycle's Scope changes log, and the result carries the cycle it left (cycleNumber, cycleLabel), where it went (movedToCycleNumber, movedToCycleLabel) and the commitment left in that cycle (commitment.items, commitment.demandDays). An item in no cycle is refused with item_not_in_cycle, one in a cycle that is not locked with cycle_not_locked (use set-cycle), one in an ended cycle with cycle_in_past, and an ended, locked or out-of-horizon destination with cycle_in_past, cycle_locked or cycle_not_found. It needs the same role as scope-change; otherwise 403 insufficient_role. Use action='undefer' on an item deferred when its plan was approved (anyforge_approve_backlog deferItemIds): it clears the deferral and the item continues as an ordinary BACKLOG item. Until then advance, begin, a forward status change, dispatch and retry are refused with work_item_deferred. Use action='dispatch' on a READY item to launch a fresh crew (omit crewId; it returns { crewId }). Pass crewType and either runProfileId or runProfileOverride to choose models per role. The initiative must accept crews: it is in progress, or operator-planned (set operatorPlanned with anyforge_update_initiative or anyforge_create_initiative when you plan the work yourself and there is no Architect plan to approve). Otherwise dispatch is refused with initiative_plan_not_approved. Use action='approve-and-route' with targetInitiativeId (and optionally milestoneId) for a request sitting in a programme's Incoming Requests bucket: it approves the request AND moves it to the initiative that will deliver it, in one write. Nothing in that bucket can be dispatched, and advance / approve_refinement / a bare status change are all refused there with approve_and_route_required. It works ONLY on an item in such a bucket — it sets status to READY, so using it to re-home an ordinary item would promote that item past its refinement approval. To move an ORDINARY item to another initiative, use action='move-initiative' with targetInitiativeId: it changes the owning initiative and nothing else (same status, assignee and approvals), inherits the destination's codebase, and drops the pinned repo and milestone placement, which named the old initiative. It works at any status, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and DROPPED included, and keeps the item's pull requests, evidence and history; it is refused while the item's crew is still running (409 move_initiative_crew_running, naming the crew: halt it or let it finish first), on an archived item (move_initiative_requires_active) and on anything still in an Incoming Requests bucket (approve_and_route_required). Use action='confirm-repo' with confirmedInitiativeId instead when the point is to ANSWER the repository question — it both re-homes the item and clears repoUnconfirmed, which a plain move deliberately does not. Use action='drop' with optional droppedReason to remove an obsolete unfinished item from the active backlog; archive is only valid after the item is DONE or DROPPED, so an archive_requires_terminal response means drop it first. Dropping an IN_PROGRESS or IN_CREW item needs confirmActiveDrop: true (a drop halts the item's crew for good); without it the drop is refused with 409 active_drop_unconfirmed, naming the status and crew. Ask the person before you send it. action='undrop' restores a DROPPED item to the status it was dropped from (BACKLOG for older drops). Status changes, drop, undrop, archive, unarchive, reopen, close-as-fixed, complete, begin, advance, dispatch, expedite and move-initiative are limited to the initiative's operator, its program's lead or owner, members of its team, the item's assignee and company Owners (the person who dropped an item may also undrop it for 7 days); anyone else gets 403 forbidden_initiative_scope and nothing is written. Every drop, restore and archive is audited with the channel it came through. Use action='close-as-fixed' with closedReason for work fixed outside AnyForge, and optionally closedEvidenceUrls (up to 10 http(s) links to the commit, pull request or release that fixed it). Use action='link-external' with externalRef { key, url? } to record where the same work lives in another system; externalRef null unlinks it. Use action='verification' with verificationState 'verified' to record that the client accepted a DONE item (it then locks), or null to stop tracking an unaccepted item; it requires a credential bound to a user (a personal key or OAuth grant) so the acceptance is attributable. Use action='add-evidence' with `evidence` to record a test run done outside AnyForge (for example a QA suite run against a sandbox) on the item, at any status; the result carries the new entry and its id. Entries are internal unless evidence.clientVisible is true. Use action='share-evidence' with evidenceId and clientVisible to share or unshare a reviewed entry. Use action='remove-evidence' with evidenceId to remove one; only its author or an owner may. anyforge_get_work_item returns the item's entries as `testEvidence`. When the item's program requires test evidence (anyforge_update_program testEvidenceRequired), action='complete' is refused with 409 test_evidence_required until the item has at least one entry of any result; add one with action='add-evidence' and complete again. close-as-fixed is not held by it. Labels (the Console's Labels field) are `tags`. Use action='update' with addTags and/or removeTags to change some labels: they apply to the labels stored at write time, need no revision, and are the way to relabel many items from a script. To replace the whole list, send tags with ifClassificationRevision, the item's classificationRevision from anyforge_get_work_item (a stale value is refused with 409 work_item_classification_modified). A labels-only update works at any status, DONE, DROPPED and archived included; other fields in the same call keep the normal edit rules. The result carries the item's labels and classificationRevision after the write. action='set-type' with type and action='set-due-date' with dueDate (yyyy-mm-dd, or null to clear) change only that field at ANY status, finished work included; action='update' refuses them once a crew has started. action='set-latest-status' with latestStatus (up to 1000 characters; null or "" clears it) writes the item's one-line current status, which clients read on shared reports; it works at any status, archived included. action='set-request-review' with requestReview 'under_review' or 'waiting_on_requester' marks a request waiting in a program's Incoming Requests (the requester sees it on the shared report); null clears it. It changes no status, is refused with 409 request_review_requires_intake_bucket on an item that is not in Incoming Requests, and is cleared when the request is routed out. anyforge_get_work_item returns requestReview, requestReviewAt and requestReviewByUid. action='accept-scope-size' with reason (why the criteria are one deliverable; required) accepts the 'split this work item' size warning on this item: it records who, when and why, stops the warning lowering the readiness score, and lapses if the criteria count grows. It needs the editor role and changes no status. action='keep-listed' keeps an unarchived DONE or DROPPED item off the program's automatic archive until it finishes again. action='checklist' applies checklistOps (all or nothing, at most 50) to the item's checklist of small steps, with ifChecklistRevision set to the checklistRevision anyforge_get_work_item returned (0 when absent; a stale value is refused with 409 work_item_checklist_modified). Each op is one of { op: 'add', text, assigneeUid?, index? }, { op: 'edit', id, text }, { op: 'toggle', id, done }, { op: 'assign', id, assigneeUid | null }, { op: 'move', id, toIndex } or { op: 'remove', id }; a list holds at most 50 steps of 300 characters. action='checklist-promote' with checklistItemId and ifChecklistRevision turns one step into a sibling work item in the same initiative, linked relates_to, and removes the step. A dropped or archived item's checklist is read-only. Requires `write` scope.

action.description: The lifecycle or field mutation to apply. Leave it out only to send `status`.

status.description: Only with NO action: move the item to BACKLOG, REFINED or READY, from one of those or from work a person began (IN_PROGRESS, no crew). This is how an item moves back (READY to BACKLOG, In progress to Backlog). Refused with 409 raw_status_not_allowed from any other status, naming allowedStatuses and useAction.

inReview.description: For action='set-review': true puts work a person began in review, false takes it back to In progress. For action='begin': true starts the item already in review.

latestStatus.description: For action='set-latest-status': the item's one-line current status, shown to clients on shared reports. Up to 1000 characters; null or "" clears it.

requestReview.description: For action='set-request-review': under_review or waiting_on_requester on a request in Incoming Requests; null clears it.

checklistOps.description: For action='checklist': the operations to apply in order, all or nothing: { op: 'add', text, assigneeUid?, index? }, { op: 'edit', id, text }, { op: 'toggle', id, done }, { op: 'assign', id, assigneeUid | null }, { op: 'move', id, toIndex }, { op: 'remove', id }. Step ids come from the item's checklist.

ifChecklistRevision.description: For action='checklist' and 'checklist-promote': the item's checklistRevision as read with anyforge_get_work_item (0 when absent). Required.

checklistItemId.description: For action='checklist-promote': the id of the checklist step to turn into a sibling work item.

assigneeUid.description: For assign/begin (and a checklist op's step owner, by uid, inside checklistOps): the human executor — a member uid or their email (anyforge_list_members lists both); null clears the assignee. assign works in any status, DONE included; only an archived item is refused. An unknown uid is refused as assignee_not_found, a person who is not an active member as assignee_not_member, a viewer or filer as assignee_role_not_eligible.

tags.description: For update: replaces every label; [] clears them. Needs ifClassificationRevision. Not with addTags/removeTags. Labels are trimmed, lower-cased and deduplicated; at most 20 per item, 40 characters each. A label in one of the workspace's label groups replaces the item's other label from that group.

addTags.description: For update: labels to add to the item's current labels. No revision needed. Labels are trimmed, lower-cased and deduplicated; at most 20 per item, 40 characters each. A label in one of the workspace's label groups replaces the item's other label from that group.

removeTags.description: For update: labels to remove from the item's current labels; one it does not carry is ignored. No revision needed.

ifClassificationRevision.description: For update: the item's classificationRevision as read with anyforge_get_work_item. Required with tags; optional with addTags/removeTags, where it is still checked.

type.description: For update or set-type: BUG, FEATURE, ENHANCEMENT, KTLO, TECH_DEBT, or INCIDENT. set-type works at any status.

priority.description: For update: P0, P1, P2, P3, or none to clear it (no priority).

allowedWritePaths.description: File write scope: a hard boundary on the repository files the crew may change, as relative patterns (literal, * or **; [ and ] are literal characters, so src/pages/[slug].astro is a valid entry). null/omitted is unrestricted; [] is read-only. Any write scope also withholds connected (MCP) tools that can write; tools their server marks readOnlyHint stay. Set before dispatch. Locked while the attached crew can still run; once it has halted or finished, send it alone in an update to change it, then retry the item. To point the crew at a monorepo folder without restricting it, use folderScope.

outOfScope.description: For update: bullet-list markdown of what this item explicitly does NOT cover; empty string clears it.

designNotes.description: For update: the design notes the crew reads beside the description (files, patterns, edge cases). Replaces the Architect's notes, so send the whole corrected text; empty string clears them. Refused once a crew is building the item.

coversCriterionIds.description: For update, at any status: the acceptance criteria of the initiative's active spec this item delivers, by criterion id (`ac-…`, listed with the spec). Replaces the list; [] clears it. An id the active spec does not hold is refused with unknown_criterion_ids, which lists the valid ones. A spec revision that only rewords a criterion carries this over on its own; set it by hand when criteria were added, removed or reordered.

plannedFiles.description: For update: the files this item is planned to change, as repository-relative paths or simple globs. Replaces the list; [] clears it. An entry that is not such a path refuses the request with invalid_planned_files. Refused once a crew is building the item.

dependsOn.description: For update: work-item ids that must finish first (Jira's 'is blocked by'). Not editable once the item is DONE or DROPPED; record history there with link-work-item.

dependencyWaits.description: For update: per dependency id in dependsOn, what this item waits for before it starts: 'merge' (the dependency's pull request merged) or 'deploy' (Done through a release or a person). null returns to the initiative's waitForDeploy. A dependency removed from dependsOn loses its choice.

crewId.description: For action='dispatch' — OPTIONAL: omit to mint a fresh crew; provide only to attach to an existing one.

crewType.description: For dispatch: the crew's type, a label (default roster and usage estimates). Every crew type runs the same Engineer-led crew and does not restrict which models run.

runProfileId.description: For dispatch: id of a saved crew run profile (Settings → Agents). Sets the provider and model for every crew role. Do not combine with runProfileOverride.

runProfileOverride.description: For dispatch: a one-off run configuration for this crew only, `{ roles: { SOFTWARE_ARCHITECT, FULL_STACK_ENGINEER, QA_REVIEWER, COMPLIANCE_SECURITY } }` where each role is `{ provider, model, reasoningEffort? }`. reasoningEffort is low, medium or high and must be one the model takes (else invalid_run_profile); absent keeps the agent's configured effort. All four roles are required (a missing one is refused with invalid_run_profile). provider is one of anthropic, openai, google, openrouter, vertex. The FULL_STACK_ENGINEER entry decides what the Engineer runs on; the other roles run when the Engineer consults them and in the review that follows a pull request the crew opened. Without a run profile, each role uses the company's Agents configuration. Do not combine with runProfileId.

closedReason.description: For action='close-as-fixed': required explanation for the external fix.

closedAsFixedByWorkItemId.description: For action='close-as-fixed': optional item that delivered the fix.

targetGithubRepo.description: For update: writable owner/name repository; null clears it where allowed. confirm-repo takes confirmedInitiativeId instead.

validationBranch.description: For update on an integration-validation item: validate this branch instead of waiting for every crew PR to merge. When it differs from the base branch, the validation run checks it out and accepts each crew PR whose head commit the branch already contains; closing the initiative still requires the merges. null or "" clears it.

sourceGithubRepo.description: For update, migration only: read-only source repository to copy from. The source fields and targetPath need it.

sourceGithubBranch.description: For update, migration only: source branch to copy from.

sourceGithubSha.description: For update, migration only: source commit to copy from.

sourcePath.description: For update, migration only: path in the source repository to copy.

targetPath.description: For update, migration only: where the copied source lands in the target repository. Not a working folder for ordinary work; use folderScope for that.

peopleDeliver.description: For update: true when people deliver this item and no crew should ever run on it (a certification, a sign-off, a meeting), though the rest of its initiative may be crew-built. Dispatch is then refused with work_item_people_deliver, the item gets no crew suggestion, and it stays ordinary open work that counts in progress. false clears it. Editable while no crew carries the item. On a task-tracker initiative every item is already people-delivered.

serviceId.description: For update: one of the initiative's services (its id). The item's repository must be the service's, and while it has one its folder comes from the service; null clears it.

folderScope.description: For update: the repository folder this item's work is in (for example apps/web), or a list when it spans several (the first picks the crew's setup and where tests run): picks which repository skills come first, and restricts nothing. Replaces the whole list; null, '' or [] clears it. Takes effect at the next dispatch.

migrationStrategy.description: For update, migration only: copy, history-preserving, or subtree.

architectPlan.description: For action='approve_refinement' only: the architect plan text recorded with the approval. action='update' does not take it.

branchName.description: For update: the branch this item's crew works on instead of the derived name. null or '' clears it back to the derived name. Takes effect at the next dispatch.

targetGithubBranch.description: For update: the base branch this item's crew branches from and opens its pull request against, instead of the initiative's source branch. null or '' clears it back to the initiative's source branch. Must exist on the remote or dispatch and retry fail with base_branch_missing. A retry of an item whose base changed after its first crew starts from the new base and reports that the existing feature branch was cut from the old one. Takes effect at the next dispatch.

continuesPullRequest.description: For update: the open pull request this work continues, as its link in the item's repository. Sets the item's branch to the pull request's head and its base branch to its base, read from GitHub, so the next crew commits to that pull request. Takes effect at the next dispatch.

dueDate.description: For update or set-due-date: ISO yyyy-mm-dd date; null clears it. set-due-date works at any status.

committedCycleNumber.description: For action='set-cycle': the cycle to commit the item to, on its own team's cadence; null takes it out of every cycle. For action='scope-change': the locked cycle to bring the item into. For action='descope': where the item goes when it leaves its locked cycle, a later unlocked cycle, or null for none.

reason.description: For action='scope-change': why this item comes into the agreed cycle. For action='descope': why it leaves it. Required for both; shown in the cycle's Scope changes log. For action='accept-scope-size': why the criteria are one deliverable; required.

confirmOverCapacity.description: For action='scope-change': true to bring the item in although the cycle goes over its team's capacity. Send only after the person saw the overage and agreed; otherwise it is refused with over_capacity_unconfirmed.

pullRequestUrl.description: For action='link-pull-request' / 'unlink-pull-request': the pull request link, https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number}.

linkedWorkItemId.description: For action='link-work-item' / 'unlink-work-item': the id of the other work item in this workspace.

parentWorkItemId.description: For action='set-parent': the id of the work item that becomes this item's parent (same program, no parent of its own).

linkType.description: For action='link-work-item' / 'unlink-work-item': relates_to, or duplicates (this item duplicates linkedWorkItemId).

estimate.description: For update: the effort estimate as a person says it — "2h", "1.5d", "1w", or a number of days. Stored as operator-days, marked operator-entered; null clears it.

estimatePoints.description: For update: the point estimate on the point scale this workspace uses (a number, or a T-shirt size such as "M"); null clears it. Refused while the workspace estimates in time.

reportedMilestoneId.description: For update: the program milestone (wave) this was reported against; null or "" clears it. Must be a milestone id of the program that owns the item's initiative.

teamSlug.description: For update: the item's own team (an existing team's slug); null or "" clears it so the item inherits its initiative's team. Allowed at any status when sent alone. The item's own team also limits who may start a crew on it (its members, owners and operators). An owner or operator can always change it; an editor only when the item has no team of its own yet or they belong to that team (else 403 forbidden_team).

droppedReason.description: For action='drop': optional operator/agent reason retained on the DROPPED item.

confirmActiveDrop.description: For action='drop': true to drop an IN_PROGRESS or IN_CREW item (its crew is halted). Send only after the person confirmed; otherwise the drop is refused with active_drop_unconfirmed.

incident.description: Incident severity and impact metadata when the item is an incident.

confirmedInitiativeId.description: For action='confirm-repo': initiative whose repository is confirmed.

targetInitiativeId.description: For action='approve-and-route': the initiative that will DELIVER this request. For action='move-initiative': the initiative the item moves to. Required for both; must not be an Incoming Requests bucket.

milestoneId.description: For action='approve-and-route': one of the TARGET initiative's existing milestone ids; omit or null to leave the item unplaced.

confirmDeclassify.description: For action='move-initiative' or 'approve-and-route' out of a PRIVATE program: the move makes the item visible to everyone who can see where it goes, so it is refused with 409 declassification_unconfirmed until confirmed. Send true ONLY after the person has explicitly said yes to that, never on your own judgement.

expedite.description: For action='expedite': true enters the expedite lane; false removes the lane flag.

blockReason.description: For action='block': what the item is waiting on. Required.

externalRef.description: For action='link-external': where the same work lives in another system, { key, url? }; null unlinks it. Do not send it with externalKey or externalUrl.

key.description: The id in the other system (e.g. PROJ-42).

url.description: Optional http(s) link to the record in the other system.

externalUrl.description: Legacy: use externalRef.url. For action='link-external': optional http(s) link to the item in the other tracker.

verificationState.description: For action='verification': 'verified' when the client accepted a DONE item; null stops tracking an item that is not yet accepted.

evidence.description: For action='add-evidence': one test run done outside AnyForge. Recorded against the key's user, or as an API key when the key is not bound to one. Secret-shaped text in summary/environment is redacted; a link carrying a credential is refused. Files (screenshots, PDFs, logs, video) attach to the entry itself in `files` as base64, at most 22 MB of files per call; larger ones go through POST …/work/{id}/evidence/uploads and are named in `uploadIds`. summary.description: What was tested and what happened. Required.

status.description: The outcome. Required. "passed" is refused when casesFailed > 0.

links.description: Absolute http(s) links to the run, report or logs.

casesPassed.description: Optional number of cases that passed.

casesFailed.description: Optional number of cases that failed.

clientVisible.description: Show this entry to the client on shared reports. Defaults to false (internal).

files.description: Files to attach to this entry, shown with it (images as thumbnails) and on the shared report when clientVisible is true.

name.description: File name with its extension, which decides the stored type.

mediaType.description: MIME type; the extension wins when they disagree.

uploadIds.description: Ids of direct uploads already confirmed for this item (POST …/evidence/uploads, PUT the bytes, POST …/uploads/{uploadId}), for files too large to send as base64.

evidenceId.description: For action='remove-evidence' or 'share-evidence': the id of the evidence entry.

clientVisible.description: For action='share-evidence': true shares the entry on client reports; false keeps it internal.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Reusing a key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reused. 8-120 letters, digits, "_" or "-".

If the prior crew record is missing, retry recovers by using the work item and initiative dispatch defaults. Returns the new crew id. If the item is DONE/DROPPED this fails with `terminal_item` — reopen it first via anyforge_update_work_item action='reopen'. Requires `write` scope.

tools.name: anyforge_list_work_item_comments
tools.description: List the discussion comments on a work item. This is separate from the transcript of any linked crew. Every comment carries a boolean `clientVisible`: true when it is shared with the client on shared reports, false when it is internal. A reply can only be shared while the comment it answers is shared (409 parent_not_shared otherwise). Same rule as the Console: requires `write` scope and a key owner who is an editor or above; a key not bound to a user is refused. Find comment ids with anyforge_list_work_item_comments.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Same rule as the Console: only the key owner's own comment can be deleted (403 not_comment_author, or comment_not_editable for Linear-mirrored and shared-report comments; 404 comment_not_found for an unknown id). A top-level comment that still has replies is refused with 409 comment_has_replies: replies are never removed or re-parented, so delete the replies first. tools.name: anyforge_list_work_item_files
tools.description: List the files attached to a work item (not files in its discussion comments): id, name, mediaType, size, clientVisible, createdAt (upload time), originalCreatedAt (when given at upload) and uploadedByUid. ONE PAGE per call (50 by default, 100 max); when meta.hasMore is true, pass meta.nextCursor back as cursor. Download a file with GET /api/v1/control/work/{itemId}/files/{fileId}.

tools.name: anyforge_add_work_item_files
tools.description: Attach up to 5 files to a work item, as the Console's Files panel does: images, PDF, text, logs, Markdown, CSV, JSON, XML, HTML pages, zip, Office documents and MP4/WebM/MOV video. SVG and other types are refused. Give each file exactly one of: text (the content as a string), contentBase64 (the bytes, base64-encoded) or path (a local file, stdio server only); name is required with text or contentBase64. Files start internal (not shared with the client). All or nothing: one refused file attaches none. One call carries at most 10 MB of request, which is about 7 MB of files once base64-encoded; for a larger file use anyforge_start_file_upload (up to 1 GB). A file already on the item with the same name and size is not attached again: it comes back with alreadyAttached: true. A same-name file of another size is refused (file_name_exists) unless onNameConflict is "keep_both". Give originalCreatedAt to keep the date a file was created in another tool. Requires the write scope and a key owner who is an editor or above. Returns { files } with each file's id. Pass an idempotencyKey to retry safely: a repeat with the same key and files returns the stored files ({ replayed: true }). Only call when the person asked to attach these files.

name.description: The file name with its extension, which decides the stored type, for example trace.log. Optional with path (defaults to the file's own name).

mediaType.description: Optional media type. The extension wins when the two disagree.

contentBase64.description: The file bytes, base64-encoded (no data: prefix).

path.description: A local file path. Stdio server only.

originalCreatedAt.description: Optional. When the file was created in the tool it came from: an ISO 8601 date or a date and time with a zone, e.g. 2024-03-01T10:22:33.000+0000. Kept beside the upload time.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional, 8-64 letters, digits, "_" or "-". A repeat with the same key and files attaches nothing new; the same key with other files is refused.

onNameConflict.description: A same-name file of a different size already on the item: refuse it (default) or attach both. A same-name, same-size file is never attached twice.

tools.name: anyforge_list_cycles
tools.description:
List a team's delivery cycles, oldest first: number, label, startDate, endDate, state (ended, active or future), isCurrent, locked and lockReason (started, or signed_off for a cycle whose plan was signed off), openReason (not_signed_off for a started cycle that is open because its team locks only at sign-off), committed (initiatives, workItems, openWorkItems and demandDays, as the Cycles board counts them) and capacity (availableDays over the cycle's own window). currentCycleNumber names the cycle containing today. By default 2 ended cycles, the current one and the next 3.

Cycle numbers count on a team's own cadence, and teams can run different cadences. To plan a work item into a cycle: read the item's team (team.id from anyforge_get_work_item), list that team's cycles, pick a cycle with locked: false, then call anyforge_update_work_item with action='set-cycle' and that number as committedCycleNumber. An item with no team uses the workspace cadence: leave team out. A locked cycle (the current cycle, and any future cycle signed off early) takes or loses work only through a scope change on the Cycles board; an ended cycle takes none. A team whose cycles lock only at sign-off (cadence.lockMode 'sign_off') keeps its current cycle unlocked until its plan is signed off, so set-cycle can add to it. Without a team, teamCadences lists the teams on a cadence of their own, whose numbers are not these.

team.description: A team slug (a work item's team.id). Its subteams' work counts too. Left out: the workspace cadence. An unknown slug is refused (unknown_team).

past.description: Ended cycles before the current one, 0–12 (default 2).

ahead.description: Future cycles after the current one, 0–6 (default 3).

tools.name: anyforge_get_timesheet_week
tools.description:
Read your own timesheet for one week (Monday to Sunday), as the Timesheets grid shows it: days; rows you can book (initiatives, then the overhead categories keyed @meetings, @admin, @support, @learning, @hiring; a program planning row keyed @program:<programId> sits with its program where you booked or were measured on it), each with days[].bookable and the reason when a day cannot take time; addable initiatives; blocked ones with the reason; and entries, every booked cell with initiativeId (or category key), date, minutes, note and source (manual = typed by a person, here or in the Console; auto = booked from a calendar or measured activity).

Read the week before anyforge_book_time and send only the cells that should change, so you do not overwrite what someone typed or a calendar booked.

date.description: Any day (YYYY-MM-DD) in the week to read. Left out: this week.

today.description: Your local date (YYYY-MM-DD), honoured within a day of UTC. Pass it when you are not on UTC, so yesterday and today mean yours.

tools.name: anyforge_book_time
tools.description: Book, change or clear cells of your own timesheet: up to 100 at once, ALL OR NOTHING. Every cell is checked by the same rules as the Timesheets grid before any is written; if one is refused, none is, and the error names it by index. A cell that already has time is replaced (mode set, the default) or added to (mode add); minutes 0 clears it; cells you do not send are left alone. Minutes are rounded to the workspace step. A day may not pass 24 hours. Refusals: not_bookable with a reason (date_in_future, period_closed, initiative_closed, no_current_quarter_key_result, not_linked, initiative_not_in_program, plan_not_agreed, not_in_agreed_plan), day_over_limit, initiative_not_found, program_not_found (program planning on a program that does not exist or that you cannot read), duplicate_entry (the same initiative and day twice), time_recording_disabled. Use the initiativeId values anyforge_get_timesheet_week lists. An empty list writes nothing and returns written: 0.

entries.description: The cells to write, each initiative and day once.

initiativeId.description: The initiative id, an overhead category key such as @meetings, or @program:<programId> for program planning.

minutes.description: Minutes for the cell. 0 clears it.

note.description: A note on the cell. Left out: the note is kept. null or "": cleared.

mode.description: set (default) replaces the minutes; add adds to them.

today.description: Your local date (YYYY-MM-DD), honoured within a day of UTC. Pass it when you are not on UTC, so yesterday and today mean yours.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Reusing a key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reused. 8-120 letters, digits, "_" or "-".

tools.name: anyforge_list_my_availability
tools.description:
List your own away spans (PTO, holiday, sick, other), earliest first, including days your calendar booked off: each with id, kind, startDate, endDate (inclusive) and note. Pass from and to to list only the spans that overlap that range. Read them before anyforge_add_my_availability, since a span that overlaps one of yours is refused.

Always your own spans, the ones Settings → Capacity → Availability lists; there is no argument that names anyone else. Needs the role that adds a span in the Console (Operator or higher). Days a span covers are not counted by the "Log your time" reminder; time already booked on them stays booked.

from.description: Only spans that end on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Only spans that start on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: anyforge_add_my_availability
tools.description:
Mark yourself away (PTO, holiday, sick or other) for every day from startDate to endDate, past or future. Refusals: availability_overlap (it shares a day with another of your spans, a calendar-created day included; conflictingEntry names it, so change that one with anyforge_update_my_availability instead), end_before_start, span_too_long (over 366 days), invalid_kind, invalid_date, insufficient_role.

Always your own spans, the ones Settings → Capacity → Availability lists; there is no argument that names anyone else. Needs the role that adds a span in the Console (Operator or higher). Days a span covers are not counted by the "Log your time" reminder; time already booked on them stays booked.

kind.description: pto, holiday, sick or other. On-call is working time and is not set here.

note.description: A short note, such as "Family trip".

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Reusing a key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reused. 8-120 letters, digits, "_" or "-".

Change one of your away spans: send only the fields that change. The result is checked as a new span would be, so an overlap with another of your spans is refused (availability_overlap). A span that does not exist is availability_entry_not_found; one that is not yours is not_own_availability_entry. Nothing is written on a refusal.

Remove one of your away spans, so its days count as working days again. A span that does not exist is availability_entry_not_found; one that is not yours is not_own_availability_entry.

tools.name: anyforge_list_initiatives
tools.description: List initiatives with status, progress and token budget/spend. ONE PAGE per call (50 by default, 100 max): the result carries `meta` with `hasMore`, `nextCursor`, `appliedFilters` (the filters that actually ran — check it when the page surprises you) and `nextAction`. When `meta.hasMore` is true, pass `meta.nextCursor` back as `cursor` with the SAME filters to get the next page. A page with no relevant rows says nothing about the remaining pages — check `meta.hasMore` before concluding there is no match. Narrow with `programId`, `repo`, `team`, `excludeGenerated`, `status` (comma-separated), `priority`, `owner`, `tag` or `search` rather than paging through a whole workspace; this is the tool that scopes a question before anyforge_list_work_items reads the items under one initiative. `search` matches code, name, description, repo and tags only. Archived initiatives are hidden unless includeArchived is set. Rows are the list projection (description is excerpted, dollar spend is omitted) — call anyforge_get_initiative for the full record.

status.description: Comma-separated InitiativeStatus filter.

programId.description: Only initiatives in this program. Pass "__none__" for the unlinked ones.

repo.description: Only initiatives whose repositories (primary or additional) include this "owner/name", ignoring case. Use it to find where work on a repository can be filed.

team.description: Only initiatives owned by this team or a team under it, by team slug. An unknown slug is refused (unknown_team).

excludeGenerated.description: true leaves out initiatives the platform created on its own: codebase-analysis drafts nobody has taken up, and the Support Triage Agent's Intake buckets. Maintenance streams stay.

owner.description: Filter by DRI uid; "me" for the API key owner, "__unassigned__" for initiatives with no DRI.

tag.description: Match initiatives carrying ANY of these tags.

search.description: Match against code, name, description, repo and tags.

sort.description: Page order (default "updated", newest first). "progress" is ranked in memory over a bounded scan, so on a very large workspace it sets `meta.truncated` — say so rather than reporting the ranking as complete.

cursor.description: meta.nextCursor from the previous page. Only valid with identical filters.

tools.name: anyforge_get_initiative
tools.description: Get an initiative with its crews, work items, lifetime spend, and daily burn-down series. Also returns `planSpecVersion` (the spec version its plan was made against), `activeSpecVersion`, `planStale` (true: the plan predates the active spec, so consider anyforge_dispatch_architect with `replan`; false: aligned; null: no verdict) and `planDriftStatus` (no_plan, no_spec, unknown, aligned or plan_predates_spec) saying why. By default (`shape: "summary"`) crews and work items are rows and initiative text longer than 1,000 characters (architect ADR, test plan, BRD) is excerpted and named in `excerptedFields`. Read one crew or work item in full with anyforge_get_crew / anyforge_get_work_item; pass `shape: "full"` only when you need every document, which can be very large. Reviewer verdicts (`architectVerdict`, `securityVerdict`, `qaVerdict`) come with `<field>Label`, the word the Console shows, and `<field>Outcome` (`clean`, `non_blocking` or `blocking`). `NEEDS_REVISION` is non-blocking and the Console labels it "Advisory"; the Console's "Needs revision" means the blocking `FAIL`.

shape.description: summary (default): rows and excerpts. full: every crew and work-item document in full.

tools.name: anyforge_get_initiative_spec
tools.description: Read an initiative's active ICE spec (Intent, Context, Expectations) with its readiness score, plus any spec submission still waiting on human review. Call before proposing a spec. `approvalGate` is what backlog approval will decide: it needs `requiredScore` (100), which is stricter than `readiness.meetsBar` (no failing checks), and `gaps` lists every check still holding the score down, warnings included.

tools.name: anyforge_propose_initiative_spec
tools.description: Submit an ICE spec for an initiative FOR HUMAN REVIEW. This does not change the active spec: a person must review it and publish it (or reject it), in the AnyForge Console section by section, or by asking you to call anyforge_publish_initiative_spec after reading it. Until then the architect and every spec gate still see the current spec — tell the user it is awaiting their review and give them the returned reviewUrl, the absolute Console link to the review page (reviewPath is the same page as a path). On an initiative with NO published spec yet, the backlog can be planned while the review is open: call anyforge_dispatch_architect with planFromPendingSpec: true. That backlog cannot be approved until this submission is published as it was planned. A newer submission replaces a pending one. Each list item may be at most 1000 characters (affectedRepos 200), counted as Unicode characters; a submission over the limit is refused with 400 spec_items_too_long, whose `violations` name every such item (field, zero-based index, length, max), so shorten or split them all at once. Only write what the user and the code support; flag open questions in `note` rather than inventing context or criteria. Requires `write` scope and an initiative-editing role.

intent.description: ICE Intent: what is being built and why — motivation, the user pain, the success measure.

context.description: ICE Context: facts about the system as it is today (one per item), not work to do.

acceptanceCriteria.description: ICE Expectations: testable, observable criteria (one per item). Required.

edgeCases.description: The "what about when X?" cases the engineer must handle.

affectedRepos.description: Read-only dependency repositories ("owner/name"), not ones the work writes to.

agentSuitability.description: How suited this work is to autonomous agents.

note.description: Note to the reviewer: sources used, assumptions, open questions (max 2000 characters).

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Reusing a key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reused. 8-120 letters, digits, "_" or "-".

tools.name: anyforge_publish_initiative_spec
tools.description: Publish a pending spec submission so it becomes the initiative's active ICE spec, exactly as it was submitted. ONLY call this when the user has read that submission (show it from anyforge_get_initiative_spec `pendingSubmission`) and explicitly asked you to publish it; never publish a spec you proposed on your own judgement. The Architect plans the whole backlog from the active spec. Pass the `submissionId` the user reviewed. Works only for a person connected through OAuth (the hosted MCP) with the `approve` scope and a role that edits initiatives; a Control API key gets 403 spec_publish_requires_person. Refused with 409 spec_version_conflict when the active spec changed after the submission, and spec_publish_needs_console_review when publishing would add the initiative's intake notes to Context (in both cases the person reviews it in the Console instead), and spec_submission_not_pending when a newer submission replaced it or it was rejected. An already published submission answers status "already_published" and changes nothing. The answer's `diff` lists each section where the published spec differs from the submission; it is always empty, because a publish whose version would differ is refused before it writes with 409 spec_publish_mismatch, carrying that diff. To accept or reject single sections, use the returned reviewUrl in the Console.

submissionId.description: The pending submission to publish: `pendingSubmission.id` from anyforge_get_initiative_spec.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Send the same key when retrying this exact call after a lost answer ("fetch failed"): the first call's result comes back and nothing is written twice. Reusing a key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reused. 8-120 letters, digits, "_" or "-".

tools.name: anyforge_approve_backlog
tools.description: Approve the proposed backlog for an initiative (HIL #1). Promotes its BACKLOG items to READY and moves the initiative to IN_PROGRESS. Pass `deferItemIds` to leave chosen proposed items out of the approval: they stay in the backlog marked deferred, are never promoted or auto-dispatched, and come back through anyforge_update_work_item action='undefer'. Refused with a 400 and nothing written when an id is not one of this plan's proposed items (defer_item_not_proposed), is the integration-validation item (defer_item_not_deferrable), would defer every item (defer_all_items), or is a dependency of an item being approved (defer_breaks_dependency). Requires `approve` scope.

deferItemIds.description: Work item ids (from anyforge_list_work_items) of proposed items to defer instead of approving.

deferReason.description: Optional reason recorded on each deferred item and in the audit trail.
